items.recapEn: At the Imagire strait Hana and Ken crossed the mouth of Lake Hamana by the bridge, talking about the old ferry and the earthquake that cut the land. Ken had left his hat in Hamamatsu and called his pack lighter. Yamada-san grilled Hamana eel, looking proud; a blue-grey cat sat on his step, and the argument happened as usual.

items.recapEn: Over grilled eel at Yamada-san's, Hana asked Ken to leave half for the cat on the step; he refused and ate down to the tail, then dropped the tail by the stone and blamed his chopsticks. Yamada-san promised to show Ken the fire. Whatever cat it is, Ken said, it eats.

items.recapEn: A sign at the old Imagire ferry landing: how an earthquake more than five hundred years ago opened Lake Hamana to the sea, how travellers crossed by boat from three landings (lords, ordinary travellers, cargo), and why the stone steps still run down into fast tidal water. Mind your step; the evening view is good.
